Titanium supply risk: H3 and H6

Model B probability improvement experiment. Forecasts describe each supplier group's change in UK titanium import-weight share.

Historical probability gates passed1/4
Current source cutoffJune 2026
Required horizons3 and 6 months

How this experiment works

Models and calibration settings were selected using forecasts up to June 2021. Calibration adjusts probability sharpness and can blend with each country's historical class frequencies. A validated share-bound rule removes mathematically impossible classes where selected.

The disruption and post-disruption periods have been reviewed in previous experiments. These are reused historical evaluations. A fresh prospective holdout is required before a production reliability claim.

Probability acceptance results

Lower Brier score is better. Acceptance requires beating both baselines and a maximum gap of 0.10 across all populated probability bins. Every bin is retained, including sparse bins.

Previous models versus this experiment

What improved and what remains

Both horizons pass the validation probability gates. Post-disruption H3 Brier falls from 0.5835 to 0.5666; H6 falls from 0.5851 to 0.5827. All four test groups beat both Brier baselines. Calibration still fails disruption H3 and both post-disruption horizons. Keep these models as experimental; the original H3 model retains the better disruption calibration.

Post-disruption H3 misses the calibration limit in a bin with 64 observations. Post-disruption H6 has a larger error in a bin with five observations. Sparse bins are still included in the required acceptance test.

Probability reliability

Points close to the diagonal indicate better reliability. Bin labels show the number of class-probability observations. Confidence is the largest class probability; it does not establish an individual prediction will be correct.

Russia disruption check

The prepared H3/H6 targets contain no Russia collapse-class event in July 2021-June 2023. This requirement remains unresolved. The frozen class boundaries are retained; source reconstruction and label design need further raw-data review.

Data and remaining requirements

Uses the existing UN Comtrade, Bank of England FX and ONS ERUC data. Supplier quantities are reconstructed from upstream shares and HS weights. Publication timing is assumed. HMRC data, 2005-2009 history and required nickel/aluminium benchmark inputs remain absent. The dataset and class boundaries are recorded in the source audit.
